dialect.detail: IBM mainframe-style COBOL; uses GOBACK, INDEXED BY, SET index, END-PERFORM, UPON CONSOLE, REDEFINES with OCCURS — all consistent with IBM Enterprise COBOL or similar mainframe dialect

purpose.domain_detail: Defect demonstration/test snippet showing a bug fix for array index handling in WORKING-STORAGE table moves
purpose.summary: This program (DF27TEST) is a test/demonstration snippet created to illustrate a specific COBOL defect (snippet 27): moving values between two indexed tables where the receiving array index was not being set. It shows both the buggy code (commented out) and the corrected code using SET to synchronize the receiving index before the MOVE.

notable_features: REDEFINES used to overlay flat table with OCCURS/INDEXED structure
INDEXED BY with SET statement to synchronize indices
Commented-out 'before' code showing the defect alongside 'after' corrected code
No file I/O despite FILE-CONTROL section present
Duplicate data-name WS-XXX-PRODUCT-CODE-4 (likely intentional defect artifact)
verdict.notes: Program is explicitly a defect demonstration snippet (REMARKS states 'COBOL SOURCE CODE FOR SNIPPLET 27 DEFECT'). The commented-out block shows the problematic code; the active block shows the fix. There is a duplicate field name WS-XXX-PRODUCT-CODE-4 which may be intentional or a typo in the test data. No COMP-3, no SQL, no CICS. Dialect is likely IBM mainframe but could compile under other dialects supporting these features.
